# Coverage matrix

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/ci/coverage-matrix.sh — do not edit by hand. CI diffs this file
     against a fresh run, so regenerate after adding a kind, a renderer, or a capability. -->

What each backend actually renders. A kind with no renderer draws a visible `⟨kind⟩`
placeholder instead of failing, so these gaps are invisible in a screenshot — the showcase
walkthrough asserts the same facts at runtime via `assert_no_placeholders`.

## External pieces

`✓` = the crate ships that backend's renderer arm; `·` = no arm, so the kind renders the
placeholder. A piece may still be absent at runtime if the app does not enable its feature.

A missing native arm may have a composed fallback, such as the core color picker.
COMPOSED from ordinary pieces, which by construction registers no renderer for its kind
([colorpicker](colorpicker.md)). This table measures arms, so it cannot see that —
nothing derived from `realize` can.

| piece | kind(s) | appkit | uikit | gtk | qt | xaml | android | arkui | dom |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`day-piece-swiftui`](/docs/reference/swiftui) | `day.piece.swiftui` | ✓ | ✓ | · | · | · | · | · | · |
| [`day-piece-text-editor`](/docs/reference/texteditor) | `day.piece.texteditor` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

## Capabilities

What each backend answers for `Cap` ([`capability()`](https://daybrite.dev/api/day_spec/trait.Toolkit.html#method.capability)): `N` native, `E` emulated, `–`
unsupported, `?` decided at runtime (day-toolkit-dom answers `NavSplit` from the viewport width;
day-toolkit-qt answers `WindowTabbing` natively on macOS alone).
An app branches on this rather than on the target name.
